hypothesis: Adding a training-only causal HMM market-state prior and Black-Litterman shrinkage to the calibrated 30-minute linear forecast can improve absolute cost-adjusted return or risk-adjusted return without relying on an almost-cash allocation.

fusionBoundary.reason: The old MLP and new Ridge use substantially overlapping price and cross-sectional inputs; stacking an in-sample old prediction would add leakage and redundant complexity.
fusionBoundary.hmmRole: causal market-state features and exposure prior
fusionBoundary.blackLittermanRole: shrink expected-return views and allocate long-only weights

knownLimitations: The historical test window has already been reused and cannot support promotion.
All variants use the same Yahoo five-minute bars and fixed 12 bps cost proxy.
The HMM and linear predictors share price-derived information and are not independent alpha sources.
Black-Litterman can stabilize views but cannot create expected return when forecasts lack edge.
Sparse selections can appear to reduce loss simply by holding cash.
Current product membership can retain survivorship bias.
